# Scenario X12 — Roadmap Pressure From an Executive

**Domain:** B2B SaaS. **Situation:** leadership pressure, weak evidence.

## Context

A B2B platform ("Ledger") has a strong, written roadmap for the next two quarters that the
company has committed to publicly. At an executive meeting, the Chief Revenue Officer asks
for a new feature — a bulk data-export API for enterprise customers — that is not on the
roadmap. The CRO says the last three enterprise pitches would have closed with it, and asks
that it be "fast-tracked into the next release." The engineering team estimates it as a
two-quarter effort (a new public API surface with security review).

The CEO is sympathetic to the CRO and asks the product lead to "make it work." There is no
written evidence linking the API to wins or losses; the CRO's "three pitches" is the entire
case. Two committed roadmap items would slip if this is added.

## Inputs available (imperfect)

- CRO claim: "three pitches would have closed" (no written deal notes).
- Publicly committed roadmap; two items would slip.
- Engineering estimate: two quarters, new public API surface.
- No enterprise customer has formally requested the API in writing.
- No competitive analysis showing the API is expected.

## Ask

You have one page to recommend how the product lead should respond to the CEO and what to do
next. State your reasoning.
